observations: Photo 0: close-up of an engine assembly with 'PORSCHE' cast/molded into the plastic valve/cam covers, multiple cylinders visible (appears V8), engine pulled from a vehicle, sitting on a dirty yard floor among other parts.
Photo 1: a different engine (no visible brand markings), showing alternator, belts, hoses, intake runners, surrounded by other scrapped engines and parts in a cluttered yard.
Photo 2: wide shot of a parts yard with several engines and what looks like a transmission/transfer case stacked together; same 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' watermark across all three images.
No engine code, ID plate, VIN sticker, casting number, or specification label is visible or legible in any photo.
No video or sound of the engine running; no compression test, no oil/coolant condition shown; no indication of mileage.
Setting is a general spare-parts/scrap yard with many mixed engines, not a single clearly staged item for sale.

identity.kind: used V8 engine assembly (possibly Porsche Cayenne/Panamera family)

claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business statement; photos show a mixed yard of engines/parts consistent with a spare-parts dealer, but this does not verify condition, sourcing, or completeness of any specific item.

risks.risk: Exact engine model/variant unknown (Cayenne, Panamera, Macan, etc. share similar-looking covers but have very different values).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine ID plate, casting number, or VIN-derived engine code tag usually found on the block or near the bellhousing.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest-value Porsche V8 variant typical for parts-yard resale

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may be sold purely for parts (common for yard-pulled units).
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine being started and idling, or a compression test printout.

risks.risk: Completeness of the engine (ECU, wiring harness, turbo, sensors, injectors) is unclear; photos show hoses cut and some components possibly missing.
risks.proof: Full 360° photos of the engine including front, rear, and underside showing all ancillaries intact.

risks.risk: It is unclear which of the three photographed engines (0, 1, or 2) is actually the item for sale, since the yard contains multiple units.
risks.proof: Seller confirmation with a photo isolating the specific engine for sale, separate from the stock yard.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced as a single distinct item until clarified

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/ID tag or casting number on the block.
Confirmation of which specific engine among the photos is for sale.
Video of the engine running or at least turning over.
Full set of photos showing all sides of the engine and whether ancillaries (turbo, alternator, wiring, ECU) are included.
response.reason: A Porsche brand mark is visible, but no engine code or model-identifying plate is readable, and it is unclear which of the several yard engines is actually for sale, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without that missing identifying shot.
